title: Real-world client-mix streaming harness with paced tokenflow and p95 regression gate
creator: Ava Kapoor
description:
Goal: build a load-testing harness that emulates a realistic mix of streaming chat clients (SSE + WebSocket) with heterogeneous token pacing, intermittent connection churn, and per-tenant KV-cache warm/cold states. The tool should focus on producing stable tokens/sec curves, p95 end-to-end latency tracking for first-byte and last-byte, and automated regression detection with signal decomposition (cold-cache vs. warm-cache vs. network variance).

Why: Existing harnesses produce high-level tokenflow numbers but fail to reproduce real-world client diversity (mobile vs. desktop, slow vs. aggressive token consumption, backgrounded clients that resume). This causes missed regressions where an optimization improves median throughput but regresses p95 for low-throughput long-tail clients.

Scope: implement a harness and analysis pipeline that can: (1) generate client mixes with configurable distributions of session length, message size, inter-token pacing, and reconnection patterns; (2) run at cluster scale (100k simulated clients) across multiple runner nodes; (3) label traces by client archetype and cache state and emit aggregated metrics (tokens/sec, p95 first-byte, p95 final-token, error-rate) per archetype and overall; (4) integrate with regression-detector to automatically create alerts and a rollback BZ when p95 increases beyond configurable thresholds.

Non-goals: provide a production traffic generator for customer traffic validation (this is for infra/regression detection only), or implement protocol-level application logic beyond what’s necessary to emulate token pacing and connection fidelity.
acceptance_criteria: Harness can emulate at least 5 client archetypes (desktop-fast, mobile-slow, background-resume, multiplexed-multiuser, flaky-network) via config files
Able to spin up 100k synthetic sessions distributed across runners with stable memory/CPU per runner (proof run on staging cluster)
Produce time-series for tokens/sec and p95 metrics broken down by archetype and cache-state (warm/cold)
Automated regression-detector integration: when p95 (first-byte) increases >15% on any archetype vs baseline, an alert and an incident BZ is created
Baseline reproducibility: repeated runs with same seed produce <5% variance in tokens/sec and <8% variance in p95
End-to-end test harness and README with runbook included in the repo and demo script for the Console dashboard
design_notes: Use a client-driver model where each simulated client is an isolated state machine with configurable token pacing and reconnection behavior
Prefer async Rust runtime for the runner nodes to maximize connection density and deterministic scheduling (we have existing runner template in ENG-142210)
Telemetry: emit OpenTelemetry spans for request lifecycle and custom tags for archetype and cache_state
Data aggregation: time-bucketed metrics pushed to Prometheus + a compressed raw trace s3 sink for offline analysis
Cost vs fidelity tradeoff: start with lightweight text stubs rather than full model responses to avoid token billing; ensure token shaping mimics length distributions
progress_updates: 2026-02-19: Kickoff meeting with infra and reliability. Agreed on archetype definitions and minimal fields for client state.
2026-02-25: Prototype runner in Rust that maintains 10k concurrent SSE sessions on a single m6i.4xlarge-equivalent test VM. Memory profile attached in drive (link).
2026-03-02: Implemented per-client pacing engine and deterministic seed control. Early runs show unexpectedly high variance for background-resume archetype — investigating jitter model.
2026-03-08: Added cache-state injection hooks to simulate cold-start and warm-cache flows. Baseline comparisons vs. warm-cache show 22% lower p95 (expected).
2026-03-12: Regression-detector integration spike complete; can post an alert to our internal monitoring when archetype p95 delta crosses threshold. Draft alert policy in PagerDuty ready.
test_plan: Unit tests for pacing engine and reconnection state machine (>= 90% coverage)
Scale runs: 10k -> 50k -> 100k sessions with incremental runner pool resizing; capture CPU/memory and socket FD usage
A/B regression test: run current runtime against runtime-1.32 candidate; capture per-archetype p95 and tokens/sec; feed to regression-detector
Chaos: introduce network delay and transient TCP resets to validate flaky-network archetype behavior
End-to-end demo: run harness for 30 minutes while streaming metrics to Console dashboard and verify alert generation
rollout_plan: Stage: run harness in staging cluster with synthetic tenants and record baseline (2-week window)
Canary: enable regression-detector alerts for non-critical tenant group; validate alert fidelity for 48 hours
Production: enable on core runtime and tie alerts to on-call and automatic rollback playbook
Post-mortem docs: link incident BZ to harness run IDs for root-cause analysis
risks: Runner resource exhaustion at target scale leading to false positives — mitigate by resource autoscaling and per-run sanity checks
Overfitting harness to current runtime behaviors (risk: missing regressions triggered by future kernels) — mitigate by varying token-length distributions and cache injection
Noise in p95 signal due to network jitter — mitigate by signal smoothing and decomposing by archetype and region
monitoring: Emit metrics: synthetic.tokens_per_sec, synthetic.p95_first_byte, synthetic.p95_last_byte, synthetic.error_rate, synthetic.connections_open
Dashboards: per-run and per-archetype panels in Grafana with run-id and seed annotated
Alerts: regression-detector webhook creates Jira BZ and PagerDuty incident when thresholds crossed
